sense: favourable, approving: of an answer, a reaction, a result

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.4: secundō populō, with the people’s approval (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly “following”, as a fair wind or the current follows a boat (see current); rēs secundae are good times, the opposite of rēs adversae.

terms.gloss: kind, favourable (of an answer or a hearing)
terms.comment: A positive answer is given benignē, kindly.

phrases.latin: nam et secundās rēs splendidiōrēs facit amīcitia et adversās partiēns commūnicānsque leviōrēs
phrases.english: for friendship makes good fortune brighter, and bad fortune lighter by dividing and sharing it

sources: Lewis & Short: secundus · Lewis & Short: benignus · Lewis & Short: benigne · Lewis & Short: prosper
